methods.paper_sections_read: 3.1.1 forward root finding; 3.1.2 implicit gradient; 3.1.3 adjoint linear solve
methods.author_core_read: weight-shared transform; no-grad forward solver; backward_hook solves J_f^T v + upstream gradient
methods.preserved: Converged input-injected equilibrium and implicit differentiation through adjoint equation; forward iterations are not in autograd graph; per-row residual/convergence/iteration diagnostics, including backward diagnostics after backward
methods.adaptation: Contractive dense tanh cell replaces author's transformer/trellis cell. Frobenius bound <=0.8 guarantees contraction. Convergence-controlled Picard replaces Broyden; paper explicitly permits any convergent black-box solver. Width equals supplied latent_dim, default 256; output is learned projection of equilibrium, not scalar-gated residual.
methods.failure_policy: Raise RuntimeError on unresolved forward or backward convergence; never silently report finite unroll as equilibrium
methods.limitations: Does not reproduce original language modeling architecture, checkpoint, dataset, pretraining or performance; no claim of Broyden implementation

methods.paper_sections_read: 2 recurrent shared attention/transition; 2.2 dynamic halting; Appendix C per-position ACT equations
methods.author_core_read: universal_transformer_act: shared recurrent attention+FFN, position/step preprocessing, halting probabilities, updates, remainders, accumulated option
methods.preserved: One shared self-attention and FFN cell repeated across depth; sinusoidal position and step timing; position-specific sigmoid halting, remaining mass, weighted accumulated output, updates/remainder diagnostics, differentiable ponder_cost = ponder_weight * mean(N+R)
methods.adaptation: Causal conversation attention; accumulated ACT option; halted tokens and their attention keys freeze exactly, with no later timing added. Forced remainder at last permitted step normalizes mass to one. Default latent_dim=256 rather than universal arbitrary 64-dimensional residual.
methods.trainer_requirement: Add module.ponder_cost to TRAIN loss. It already includes ponder_weight=0.01 by default.
methods.limitations: No machine translation encoder-decoder reproduction; recurrent weights are shared but autograd retains finite ACT iterations; no accuracy/generalization claims

methods.paper: Neural Relational Inference for Interacting Systems, ICML 2018
methods.paper_sections_read: 3.1 encoder node-edge-node factor graph; 3.2 categorical sampling; 3.3 typed decoder; 3.6 variational training
methods.author_core_read: MLPEncoder node2edge/edge2node factor graph and posterior logits; MLPDecoder separate message networks for edge categories, skip_first no-edge, receiver aggregation and residual dynamics prediction
methods.preserved: Amortized categorical latent edges, node-edge-node factor encoder, hard straight-through Gumbel sampling in TRAIN, posterior expectation in EVAL, explicit type-zero no-edge, distinct message network per nonzero edge category, interaction decoder, next-utterance generative feature prediction plus uniform-prior categorical KL
methods.adaptation: Nodes are actual current/past utterance representations with variable prefix length, not five fixed Base/Gap roles. Graph candidates cover directed distinct utterance pairs. Prefix at t contains only t and earlier nodes. Original persistent multi-object trajectory dynamics becomes utterance succession prediction, so this is a domain adaptation, not an exact NRI reproduction.
methods.causality: Future local[t+1].detach() is consulted solely as TRAIN auxiliary prediction target. EVAL prediction loss is zero. Forward hidden[t] and edge posterior at t never depend on future input. Separate no-history singleton decoder has no fabricated edge.
methods.trainer_requirement: Add module.auxiliary_loss to TRAIN loss; includes prediction_weight=1 and kl_weight=0.01. Do not treat plain supervised task loss alone as complete NRI objective.
methods.limitations: One-step generative objective may suffer degenerate decoders; original multi-step object rollout and physical graph recovery are not reproduced. All-prefix computation is O(L^3) summed pair work and is unbenchmarked on long conversations. No graph truth or interpretability claim. Task feature prediction variance is implicit fixed variance (MSE), not copied physical-unit likelihood scaling. KL is mean categorical KL per edge, then mean over non-singleton conversation prefixes, not the author's per-object normalization.

methods.paper: This Looks Like That: Deep Learning for Interpretable Image Recognition, NeurIPS 2019
methods.author_core_read: class-specific prototype identity, sigmoid feature head, squared L2 distances, log similarity, bias-free class head; nearest same-class training patch push; CE+0.8 cluster-0.08 separation+1e-4 wrong-class L1
methods.implementation: PrototypeClassifier; standalone full classifier/projection API rather than pretending prototypes are a generic regression residual readout
methods.preserved: Trainable class-specific prototypes; squared feature distance and logarithmic similarity; class head initialized +1 for same class and -0.5 for others; CE, cluster, separation and wrong-class L1 regularizers; exact nearest same-class TRAIN feature exemplar projection with stable source IDs and atomic missing-class failure
methods.adaptation: Each utterance representation is one prototype feature patch instead of an image spatial patch. Input projection uses sigmoid to preserve bounded feature domain. No claim of anatomical/image-part interpretation.
methods.projection_api: project_train_exemplars(batches, split='train'), batches yield (input[N,D], labels[N], stable IDs); split other than train rejected. Caller supplies actual TRAIN-only rows under current encoder; provenance is stored in projection_records. Reproject after encoder changes before presenting prototypes as exemplars.
methods.task_change: MOSI continuous sentiment MSE is not ProtoPNet's classification task. Run explicit binary sentiment classification and compare against a matched binary baseline. Preserve the established positive/nonpositive label convention and all dataset split rules; original MSE baseline comparisons cannot establish a faithful ProtoPNet result.
methods.trainer_requirement: Use classification CE via PrototypeClassifier.loss; implement warm/joint/projection/head schedule and store projection provenance. Root owns trainer integration. Missing projection or regression-only training is incomplete C17, not a faithful prototype experiment.
methods.limitations: No TRAIN schedule or real-data projection was executed by this module task; CPU synthetic projection verification is not an experimentally projected trained model
